text:
B: Hiya! Oh, sorry, hi. Can you hear me okay?
A: Yeah. Hi. I'm Bethany.
B: I'm Chloe. Sorry, I'm a bit nervous, I don't know why, it's only three minutes.
A: No, me too. I've done one already and I still am.
B: Oh, how was it?
A: It was okay. He was nice, sort of. He just didn't say loads. Well, he did, but... I'm not sure really.
B: Oh, I think I know who you mean, from the photos. Erm. Where are you from?
A: Bridgwater. In Somerset.
B: Oh, nice. I'm in Bloxwich, which is Walsall, kind of near Birmingham. Probably means nothing to you.
A: Not really, sorry.
B: No, that's fine, it doesn't mean much to anyone! What do you do?
A: I'm looking for work at the moment. I volunteer in a charity shop, the hospice one. What about you?
B: I'm at uni, third year, primary teaching. So I'm about to do my last placement, which I'm kind of terrified about, to be honest. I've done Year 2 and Year 4, and the kids were lovely, it's not the kids. It's more the staff room. Everyone's been there twenty years and they all know where they sit, and you're stood there with your mug like, can I... is this anyone's chair? Sorry, I'm rambling.
A: No, you're not. I'd be scared of the staff room too.
B: It's the worst bit! Honestly, give me thirty six-year-olds any day.
A: Are those picture books behind you?
B: Yeah! I've been collecting them for my classroom, like, when I get one. Some of them are from charity shops, actually. The illustrations in some of them are just gorgeous, the kids stare at them for ages.
A: I love picture books. I sort of draw, a bit. Birds, mostly.
B: Oh, was that your robin? In your photo? I thought that was lovely.
A: Oh. Yeah, that was mine. Thank you. I do pencil and fineliner, mostly what I see by the river or out on the Levels. I'd love to illustrate a nature book one day. Like a proper one, with all the birds in. But I don't know, I'm not really... I'm not sure I'm good enough to call myself an artist. Sorry, that's a bit much.
B: No, it's not! You totally should. Kids would love that. They go mad for birds, honestly. We did a birdwatch in Year 2 and one boy cried because he saw a blue tit.
A: Aw. That's really sweet.
B: He was so happy. Erm, yeah. That's it really.
A: ...
B: Sorry, what else do you like doing?
A: Reading. Walking. And I bake when I can't sleep. I made flapjacks at about two this morning.
B: Oh my God, same. I bake when I'm stressed. I'm doing banana bread tonight for placement prep, but I've got to wait until my mum's done tea.
A: I do banana bread too! Kieran says he's sick of it.
B: Kieran? My brother's called Kieran! He's seventeen, he eats all the crisps.
A: Mine's my boyfriend. He's on nights this week, so it's just me and the smell of chips from downstairs.
B: Chips?
A: We live above a takeaway. It's sort of nice, sometimes, and sometimes it's—
